sentences.text: As held above, the deceased Tejpal was having his wife, 03 sons (2 married and one unmarried) and 02 daughters dependent upon him on the date of the incident.

Furthermore, it is apparent on record that apart from the wife of the deceased and his two unmarried daughters and one son, other petitioners namely Gautam and Sunny being married sons were not dependent on the deceased as they are having their own independent income and are maintaining their large families separately.

Therefore,
the remaining four original petitioners shall be treated as dependents of the deceased for the purpose of the present petition.
Furthermore, since there were total 04 dependents of the deceased, hence, 1/4th of the earnings of the deceased Tejpal shall be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
Therefore, in the entire given facts and circumstances, deduction of 1/4th of total income is made for personal living expenses of deceased.
Hence, an amount of Rs. 2,754/- (Rs. 11,017/4) is required to be deducted from annual income of deceased.

Finally, annual dependency of dependents is calculated as under (annual income) - (annual expenses of deceased) i.e. (Rs. 1,32,204/- - Rs.
33,048/-) = Rs. 99,156/- per annum.
